newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - SeaChange to spend heavily on R&D - CFO.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - SeaChange to spend heavily on R&D - CFO.

text.p: SeaChange International Inc's chief financial officer told Wall Street analysts it plans to spend a million dollars more in each upcoming quarter this year than analysts forecasted on research and development, which would cut into upcoming earnings.

Joseph Tibbetts said SeaChange plans to spend roughly $3.4 million in each of the third quarter and the fourth quarters, while Wall Street analysts' had expected spending of about $2.4 million. That will hurt earnings by about $0.05 a share in each of the quarters, he said.

"There's an awful lot of opportunity, and we think it's a good investment. But it means some analysts had to cut their short-term models and reduce earnings estimates," Tibbetts told Reuters in a telephone interview.

The company first told analysts of the increased R&D expenditures in a conference call after the release of its second quarter earnings, prompting some analysts to downgrade the stock's rating despite its strong quarterly results. Net income was $2.4 million or $0.18 a share, up from $1.4 million or $0.12 last year.
The stock dropped sharply, losing about 30 percent of its value. Shares were off 8-1/2 to 19-3/8 in afternoon trading.
SeaChange topped the list of net losing stocks on the Nasdaq on a percent basis.
SeaChange provides software that allows cable operators and television broadcasters to digitally store videos like advertisements and news updates and insert them quickly into TV network streams.

This allows cable operators, who have often survived on subscription revenues, to generate ad revenues. He said SeaChange is also working on technology that allows cable systems to insert ads into interactive systems such as pay-per-view and video-on-demand services.

"We think we have an 83 percent market share in the United States in terms of digital ad insertion. The industry is moving very rapidly from tape-based systems to digital, and ... we want to stay well ahead technically and move more into the interactive services," Tibbetts said.

Alex. Brown & Sons Inc analysts Philip Rueppel and Michael Carboy said in a report that he was cutting the stock's investment rating to "market performer" due to its high valuation, 44 times 1998 earnings per share, and because it has performed so strongly.
SeaChange went public in November for $15 each and was nearly double that, closing Tuesday at at $27-7/8, before the stock's dramatic fall today. The stock has been as high as 39-1/2.

Analysts said a slight deterioration of the balance sheet and softer-than-expected international sales also muted the strong revenue growth in the fiscal second quarter and contributed to the downgrade on a near-term basis. On a longer-term, they said they would look for signs that the company's new products were gaining acceptance.
